status: draft - agree with A, C, D, E before implementing
rule: Any change to a feature name, its order, its transform or a vocabulary bumps feature_version. Models store the feature_version they were trained on; the backend refuses inference input whose feature_version differs from the active model's.

event_types._doc: Allowed events.event_type values and their collection layer. Source-specific fields go to events.payload.

forbidden_as_features._doc: Never feed these to a model. They identify WHO/WHEN, not WHAT, so the model memorizes the lab setup instead of learning attacks. IPs may be used as graph node identity (Task D) but never as numeric/categorical inputs.
fields: suricata alert signature (it is another detector's answer)

categorical_vocabularies._doc: Fixed vocabularies -> one-hot in exactly this order. Unseen values map to 'other'; missing to 'none' (service only).

flow_features._doc: One vector per flow (Zeek conn.log row). Stored in flows.features, used as GAT edge features. Order below is the vector order.

window_features._doc: One vector per (device, window). Stored in feature_windows.features. Input to LSTM-AE / VAE. Order below is the vector order.
window_features.empty_window_rule: Inside a capture, a window with no events is REAL zero activity -> all counts 0 (valid). Outside captures nothing is generated; sequences never cross capture boundaries.

numeric.name: n_unique_dst_port
numeric.from: distinct dst_port on the device (scans light this up)

numeric.name: ratio_failed_conn
numeric.from: share of conns with conn_state in {S0,REJ,RSTOS0,RSTRH,SH,SHR,OTH}; 0 if no conns

numeric.name: mean_conn_duration
numeric.from: mean duration_s of inbound conns; 0 if none

numeric.name: n_ssh_telnet_conn
numeric.from: inbound conns with service ssh/telnet or dst_port in {22,23,2222,2223}

numeric.name: n_mqtt_publish
numeric.from: count events mqtt_publish (excluding the device's own telemetry topic)

numeric.name: sensor_n_readings
numeric.from: count sensor_reading (a DoS'd ESP32 sends fewer); 0 for non-sensor devices

numeric.name: sensor_smoke_delta_max
numeric.from: max |change| between consecutive smoke readings; 0 if <2 readings

numeric.name: sensor_temp_delta_max
numeric.from: max |change| between consecutive temperature readings; 0 if <2 readings

numeric.name: sensor_humidity_delta_max
numeric.from: max |change| between consecutive humidity readings; 0 if <2 readings

scaling.method: sklearn StandardScaler on numeric columns whose scale = 'standard', AFTER the transform; one-hot and scale = 'none' columns pass through unchanged
scaling.fit_on: TRAIN split, label = 0 rows only (the normal traffic the autoencoders learn from)
scaling.never_fit_on: validation, test, or any attack data

artifacts._doc: Published by B for every feature_version; C/D load these, never re-fit their own.

files.flow_scaler.joblib: fitted scaler for flow numeric features
files.window_scaler.joblib: fitted scaler for window numeric features
files.feature_order.json: {"flow": [41 names], "window": [24 names]} - the exact column order of every vector
files.contract.json: copy of this file as it was at fit time

labeling.flow_rule: label = 1 if attacker_ip is src_ip OR dst_ip AND ts_start is within [start_ts, end_ts] of a run; scenario/run_id copied from the run. Every other flow inside a capture = 0. SQL: CALL label_capture('<capture_id>')
labeling.event_rule: same rule on events.ts and events.src_ip/dst_ip
labeling.window_rule: label = 1 if any labeled-1 flow or event touches the device in that window; scenario = the scenario with the most attack rows in the window
labeling.live_data: label = NULL (unlabeled) until an analyst labels the alert (alerts.analyst_label)
labeling.clock_rule: All devices NTP-synced; all timestamps stored as UTC. Attack logs record start/end in UTC with a 2-second safety margin added on each side.

splits.unit: whole capture or whole attack run - NEVER random rows (neighbouring flows are near-duplicates; random splits leak and inflate scores)
splits.train: ~70% of capture time, chronologically first; models C use only its label = 0 rows
splits.validation: ~15%, used to choose thresholds and early stopping
splits.test: ~15%, chronologically last; must contain at least one run of every scenario
splits.zero_day_holdout: optional: hold one scenario (e.g. mqtt_spoofing) out of train/val entirely, test-only

outputs._doc: Dataset exports B delivers (parquet = pandas.read_parquet / numpy.load). All under data/processed/v{feature_version}/.

arrays.X: float32 [N, T, F] with T = 30 windows (5 minutes), F = 24
arrays.y: int8 [N] - 1 if any window in the sequence is an attack
arrays.y_window: int8 [N, T] - per-window labels (for point-wise evaluation)
arrays.window_start: datetime64 [N] - start of the first window

sequences_{split}.npz.rule: consecutive windows of ONE device inside ONE capture; never crosses captures

columns: <41 flow feature columns as edge features>
edges_{split}.parquet.node_id_rule: default: 'dev:<device_id>' if the IP belongs to a known device, else 'ip:<address>'. Optional service nodes 'svc:<device_id>:<port>/<proto>' are D's choice - raw columns are included so D can rebuild the graph any way.
edges_{split}.parquet.ts: float seconds since epoch (UTC), sorted ascending

alert_format._doc: What D's inference writes via POST /api/v1/alerts and E reads via GET /api/v1/alerts/{id}. Mirrors the alerts table.
